task.description: Root-cause diagnosis (diagnosis only, not the fix) of ISS-0418: implement the OQ-5 operator-configurable cap on concurrently in-flight WASM invocations -- the structural root fix for ISS-0352's recurring wasmex native-thread-pool exhaustion class (6+ independent recurrences: PR #691, #780/ISS-0392, #786/ISS-0400, #790/ISS-0401, #795/ISS-0406, #810/ISS-0404, always contained to the isolated `mix test --only wasm_hang` CI subprocess, main suite always green, but chronically blocking merges via 60-180s ExUnit timeouts under runner contention -- this exact flake was hit repeatedly by ORCH this session too, rerun-and-pass each time). Read docs/issues/ISS-0352.yaml and docs/issues/ISS-0406.yaml in FULL for the complete recurrence history, and lib/letflow/design/req170-wasm-wallclock-timeout.md section 8 (OQ-5) plus the referenced decision 0014-*.md for the already-scoped-but-unimplemented fix direction, before diagnosing. Determine: (1) exactly where wasmex invocations are dispatched in the current codebase (the actual call site(s) that would need to acquire a permit before invoking a WASM guest), (2) what mechanism should own the cap (a global semaphore? a bounded worker pool? an existing rate-limiter primitive already in this codebase, e.g. Letflow.Admission from REQ-216/218/ISS-0431?), (3) how the cap should be operator-configurable (a config value, following this project's existing config conventions), and (4) whether this genuinely needs to apply only to the isolated wasm_hang test subprocess or to the wasmex invocation path generally (the acceptance criteria's own wording says 'and/or', meaning this is not yet settled and diagnosis should recommend one). Hand off a clear, well-evidenced recommendation to CODE-DESIGNER.
